signals.verification_issue: Article 4 discusses Hugging Face (third-party platform), not Meta. While deepfake abuse is documented, attributing this as a Meta-specific regulatory/moderation risk is unsupported by the source material.

analysis.summary: The articles reveal a pivotal shift in digital discovery: AI tools like ChatGPT are displacing traditional SEO and organic search, creating significant competitive pressure on Google's core search business while benefiting Microsoft's OpenAI partnership. However, emerging concerns around AI-generated deepfakes and non-consensual content present regulatory and reputational risks for platforms hosting generative AI models, particularly Meta and open-source repositories. The broader AI infrastructure market remains constructive, but the battle for AI-driven search monetization and platform governance will define tech valuations in 2025-2026.
risks: Regulatory crackdown on generative AI misuse and deepfake creation could increase compliance costs across sector
Accelerating shift from search advertising to AI-driven discovery threatens Google's primary revenue model

articles.title: On 4th try, Outlook scores FDA nod for reformulated version of Roche's Avastin for AMD
articles.summary: Roche’s cancer treatment Avastin has long been employed as an off-label option for wet age-related macular degeneration patients. Now the FDA has endorsed a new formulation of the VEGF inhibitor for regulated use in the U.S. Bringing it to the market is Outlook Therapeutics, which labored through three FDA rejections to finally secure a nod. It will be known commercially as Lytenava.
